statement: For any finite oriented path that neither starts nor ends at a square-medial vertex, the displayed spin-one relation F_NW-F_SE=i(F_NE-F_SW) holds when F_e=E[e^{iW(e,b)}1_{e in gamma}] and W is signed turning from the oriented edge direction to the terminal direction; it follows solely from path flux conservation and cannot identify an SLE limit.
assumptions: Incident incoming directions d_NW=u, d_SE=-u and outgoing directions d_NE=i*u, d_SW=-i*u
Each oriented edge is traversed at most once; path does not start or end at tested vertex
source: Independent algebraic rederivation of w594-C0049-L1; source convention not yet independently matched to primary paper
proof_or_counterexample: Multiply F_NW-F_SE-iF_NE+iF_SW by u/d_b. Coefficients become +1,+1,-1,-1 on NW,SE,NE,SW respectively. Each path visit has one incoming and one outgoing edge, so their summed indicators agree pathwise; expectation preserves equality. This argument holds for an arbitrary deterministic path law, including a fixed nonscaling path.
remaining_gap: Verify that the published FK observable uses these exact oriented-edge and winding conventions; this result does not settle C0049.

statement: On one fixed finite FK Dobrushin graph with m edges, v vertices, fixed wiring, and |W|<=L, |D_h-G_0|<=h L^2/2+L(exp(pi^2(m+2v)h^2/4)-1) for 0<h<=1/2; no mesh-uniform conclusion follows.
assumptions: Same configuration space and exploration map at all h
source: w594 ATTEMPT.md Lemma 2; FK weight formula arXiv:1208.3787v2 Eq. (2.1)
proof_or_counterexample: Put c=cos(pi h/2). Removing common (1-p_h)^m, each weight relative to h=0 is c^r, r=o+2k in [0,m+2v]. The normalized density lies in [c^N,c^(-N)]. Taylor gives |(exp(-ihW)-1)/(-ih)-W|<=h W^2/2. For Y=W exp(iW)I, expectation shift is at most L(c^(-N)-1); -log cos x<=x^2 on [0,pi/4]. Linearity gives the endpoint local relation.
remaining_gap: No mesh-uniform N or winding moment estimate; no slit-domain observable convergence or SLE identification.

statement: The spin-one local equation, |F|<=1 and F(e_b)=1 do not force an SLE(4) scaling limit for arbitrary oriented path laws.
assumptions: Path law need not be FK
source: w594 ATTEMPT.md counterexample; independent orientation construction
proof_or_counterexample: On the diagonal medial grid, type A vertices have outgoing NE/SW and neighboring type B vertices outgoing NW/SE. Repeat NE then SE: two steps move east and the directed path stays within one mesh of a horizontal diameter. A deterministic law satisfies local flux and normalization yet converges to a Dirac diameter; SLE(4) has Brownian, non-Dirac Loewner driving.
remaining_gap: Refutes equation-only identification, not critical FK convergence.

statement: For abstract deterministic W_n=2 pi n and h_n=1/(2n), the first-order spin quotient has relative error sqrt(1+4/pi^2)>1 despite h_n tending to zero.
proof_or_counterexample: h_n W_n=pi and exp(iW_n)=1, so D_n=(-1-1)/(-i/(2n))=-4in and G_n=2 pi n; divide their complex distance by 2 pi n.
remaining_gap: Actual FK winding distributions need separate control.

statement: Theorem 1.2 of arXiv:2610.08507v1 proves q=4 p=2/3 free-boundary FK loop convergence to CLE(4), not expressly C0049's marked Dobrushin interface limit.
assumptions: Direct comparison of theorem hypotheses and conjecture wording
No implication across boundary conditions assumed
proof_or_counterexample: Theorem 1.2 specifies free boundary conditions, entire loop collection and Camia-Newman topology; Conjecture 3 specifies Dobrushin domains, marked path and chordal SLE. Their statements differ.
remaining_gap: Other implications or proofs of the q=4 Dobrushin case not established by this comparison; openness UNKNOWN.

statement: Replace the pending author-page observation with the exact arXiv:2610.08507v1 Theorem 1.2 scope: q=4 p=2/3 free-boundary loop convergence in the Camia-Newman topology; no marked Dobrushin path claim is stated.
assumptions: No unproved implication across boundary conditions
proof_or_counterexample: Compared boundary conditions, object and convergence topology in both primary statements. The new theorem concerns free-boundary loops; the conjecture concerns a Dobrushin exploration path.
remaining_gap: Whether the loop result plus other methods settles marked q=4 path convergence remains unverified; current openness UNKNOWN.
